Convergence and Grace in Dynamic Systems

The paper studies how repeated interactions approach stable behavior over time.

It argues that boundary conditions shape how quickly a system converges and how sensitive it is to disturbance.

The discussion compares physical attractors with theological language for sustained order and correction.
